transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Nice to meet you, Dr. Smith. I came in because, well, my mind just feels really foggy lately. I do clerical work at a library, and... I can't even keep my place in my old cataloguing notes anymore. It's gotten to the point where I just sit there and I can't even decide what simple thing to do next. It's making it hard to get through the day.
Beyond the mental fogginess, have you been feeling sad, down, or have you lost interest in the things you usually enjoy?

Yes, I have. Um, most days lately, I just sit at the kitchen table... and it feels like the color has just gone out of everything. Even my old watercolor books, which I usually like, they just make me feel heavy now instead of interested. I just don't have it in me to care about them right now.
Have you ever experienced a period like this in your life before, or is this the first time you have felt this way?

I'm not really sure, to be honest. I mean... I've had times in the past where I felt a bit down, just like anyone else, I suppose. But I don't think I've ever had a stretch quite like this. I can't remember ever feeling this... stuck and foggy before. So, I guess this would be the first time it's been this bad.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your sleep patterns since you started feeling this way?

Well, yes, my sleep has been pretty messed up. I'll go to bed feeling completely exhausted, but then I always seem to wake up around four in the morning. And once I'm up, that's it. I just lie there in the dark, staring at the ceiling, trying to figure out what I'm even supposed to do with myself now. I just can't get back to sleep after that.
When you are sitting at the table feeling this way, do you feel like your movements have slowed down significantly, or do you feel a sense of restless agitation where you can't sit still?

It's definitely the first one. I don't feel restless at all, my whole body just feels... slow. It's like even doing simple things, like walking down to the corner store or just sorting papers on my desk at work, it all just takes so much more effort than it should right now.
Have you noticed any change in your appetite or your weight since you started feeling this way?

Yeah, there's definitely been a change there. I actually have to remind myself to eat these days. My wife has noticed it, too... she points out that I'm leaving my rice and soup half-finished at dinner. And that's just not like me. Before all this, I would never waste a meal. I just don't really have the desire to eat right now.
Do you feel like you are still able to carry out your daily responsibilities, even if it takes a lot of effort, or do you feel completely unable to function or perform your basic tasks at all?

Well, I wouldn't say I'm completely unable to do anything, but... I'm definitely not keeping up with my responsibilities. I've just let a lot of things pile up lately. Like, uh, the lecture plans, travel notes, and even just simple household paperwork... it's all just sitting in stacks right now. I just can't reliably organize myself the way I used to, so it's getting pretty hard to function normally.
Have you noticed any other physical changes, such as feeling like your digestive system has slowed down, or perhaps experiencing a sense of worthlessness or excessive guilt?

Well, no, I haven't really noticed any changes with my digestion. Everything seems pretty normal on that end, aside from just not having the desire to eat. 

And as for feeling worthless or guilty... no, not really. I mean, I don't like that I'm leaving all my paperwork in stacks and falling behind at the library, but I don't feel a sense of deep guilt over it. I don't feel worthless, I just... I mostly just feel too drained to get it all done right now.
